title: Fix 32-bit build failure due to `statFlagMap` using int keys
body:
Change `statFlagMap` from `map[int]string` to `map[uintptr]string` and remove int/uintptr casts in `statFlagNames()`, matching `mountFlagMap`. On 32-bit architectures, `unix.MS_NOUSER` (0x80000000) overflows signed int.

Regression from PR #6129.

Fixes this podman cross build failure:
```
# go.podman.io/buildah/chroot
Error: vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/chroot/run_linux.go:63:3: cannot use unix.MS_NOUSER (untyped int constant 2147483648) as int value in map literal (overflows)
make: *** [Makefile:512: bin/podman.cross.linux.arm] Error 1
Error: Process completed with exit code 2.
```
Link: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/30037831733/job/89310129440?pr=29242

comments.body: I am supposed also with cross build failure in podman. Maybe I did something wrong with rebase or vendoring. But it occurred after vendoring container-libs.

@Honny1 yes see my comment on podman-dev, the vendoring you did there did downgrade buildah to 1.44.0 which does not carry the fix, you want to make sure it has the latest buildah on the branch as well. The go mod version selection is sometimes broken and picks an older version because it does not understand the branching rules we use.

We check cross-compiles to linux/arm in CI, and it passed in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/actions/runs/29934820816/job/89006023462#step:4:16, so that's not a problem we're having on main.
@Luap99 @nalind It was a vendor issue on my side. Let me know if we still want this change, but I think we can close it.
